items.title: Section: Deeds Four Through Six — Silencing Every Rival Doctrine, Equanimity Towards Every Disciple, and Matching Word to Deed

items.zh: 又諸如來普能降伏一切他論，普能成立一切自論。是名如來第四作事。如是作事，四無所畏所能成辦。又諸如來所化有情，於佛教勅若正安住、不正安住，如來於彼心無雜染，是名如來第五作事。如是作事，三種念住所能成辦。又諸如來如自所言，即如是作。是名如來第六作事。如是作事，三種不護所能成辦。
items.en:
Fourth, the fourth deed. The Tathāgatas universally subdue every rival doctrine and universally establish their own teaching; this is called the Tathāgata's fourth deed. This deed is accomplished through the four fearlessnesses.
Fifth, the fifth deed. Whether the beings the Tathāgatas teach correctly abide by the Buddha's instruction or not, the Tathāgata's mind remains free of defilement towards them; this is called the Tathāgata's fifth deed. This deed is accomplished through the three foundations of mindfulness.
Commentary: as for correctly abiding or not correctly abiding — those wholly correct in conduct are correctly abiding; those wholly incorrect are not correctly abiding; those of mixed conduct are both correctly and not correctly abiding. This should be understood as covering all three assemblies together.
Sixth, the sixth deed. The Tathāgatas act exactly as they themselves have taught; this is called the Tathāgata's sixth deed. This deed is accomplished through the three things requiring no guarding.

items.title: Section: Deeds Seven Through Ten — Watching the World Day and Night, Never Abandoning a Task, Perfect Deportment, and Inexhaustible Benefit

items.zh: 又諸如來常以佛眼，於晝夜分遍觀世間，是名如來第七作事。如是作事，如來大悲所能成辦。又諸如來頓於一切一切作事皆無退捨，是名如來第八作事。如是作事，無忘失法所能成辦。又諸如來所行儀軌，如實隨轉，無越作用。是名如來第九作事。如是作事，永害習氣所能成辦。又諸如來於其能引無義聚法、於不能引有義聚法、亦不能引無義聚法，簡擇捨離；於其能引有義聚法，為眾宣說、開示、顯發；是名如來第十作事。如是作事，一切種妙智所能成辦。如是如來由前所說百四十種不共佛法，能作如來一切所作一切佛事。如是佛事若廣分別不易可數，乃至俱胝那庾多百千大劫說不能盡。
items.en:
Seventh, the seventh deed. The Tathāgatas constantly survey the entire world, day and night, with their buddha-eye; this is called the Tathāgata's seventh deed. This deed is accomplished through the Tathāgata's great compassion.
Eighth, the eighth deed. The Tathāgatas never retreat from or abandon any task at all; this is called the Tathāgata's eighth deed. This deed is accomplished through the dharma of never forgetting.
Ninth, the ninth deed. The Tathāgatas' deportment unfolds truthfully, never overstepping its function; this is called the Tathāgata's ninth deed. This deed is accomplished through the permanent destruction of habitual tendencies.
Tenth, the tenth deed. The Tathāgatas discern and cast aside the heap leading towards the meaningless and what leads towards neither the meaningful nor the meaningless, while teaching, revealing, and expounding the heap leading towards the meaningful; this is called the Tathāgata's tenth deed. This deed is accomplished through wisdom of every kind.
Second, vast and inexhaustible. Thus the Tathāgata, through the aforementioned one hundred forty exclusive buddha-qualities, accomplishes every deed a Tathāgata performs. Were these deeds analysed in detail, they would be uncountable, inexhaustible even across koṭis of nayutas of hundred-thousands of great eons of description.

items.title: Section: Why Called "Established," and Why Called "Unshared" — Even With Bodhisattvas Who Merely Resemble the Real Thing

items.zh: 如是所說諸如來住、諸如來地，名為建立。何以故？依此住此希求品類諸菩薩眾，於菩薩學能正修學，亦依住此而有所證，即依住此普能成辦一切有情一切義利，是故說此名為建立。又此一切所說佛法，於利他事最為隨順，一切如來是利他事之所顯現，聲聞、獨覺則不如是。是故說名不共佛法。又於如是諸佛法中，自有佛法，聲聞、獨覺一切一切皆所不得。所謂大悲、無忘失法、永害習氣、一切種妙智。自有佛法雖分似得，而一切種皆不圓滿。如來於彼一切一切悉皆證得，於一切種無不圓滿，最極超過，最極殊妙，是故皆說名為不共。
items.en:
Fourth, naming; first, "established"; first, stating. This aforementioned Tathāgata abiding and Tathāgata ground is called "established."
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining. Because in reliance on this abiding, bodhisattvas of aspiring kind correctly train in the bodhisattva training, attain realisation in reliance on it, and universally accomplish every benefit for every being in reliance on it — for this reason it is called "established."
Second, "unshared"; first, excluding only the two vehicles. All these qualities accord most fully with benefiting others; every Tathāgata is what benefiting others makes manifest, while śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are not so; therefore these are called unshared buddha-qualities.
Second, excluding everything further; first, explaining the name; first, excluding; first, excluding the two vehicles. Among these buddha-qualities, some belong to the Buddha alone, attained by neither śrāvaka nor pratyekabuddha in any respect: namely, great compassion, the dharma of never forgetting, the permanent destruction of habitual tendencies, and wisdom of every kind.
Second, excluding bodhisattvas. Though bodhisattvas may resemble a portion of these qualities, none is brought to full perfection in every respect; the Tathāgata alone has realised all of them, perfect in every respect, utterly surpassing, utterly excellent.
Second, concluding. Therefore all of these are called unshared.

items.title: Section: Five Ways a Bodhisattva Is Called the Buddha's Own Child — and the Entire Bodhisattva Stage Now Complete

items.zh: 當知此中，獨一有義是不共義。如是圓滿顯示一切菩薩學道及學道果，名菩薩地。具說一切菩薩學道及學道果，一切種教實依處故。
items.en:
Second, revealing the meaning. Know that here, being possessed by one alone is what "unshared" means.
Commentary: as for bodhisattvas partially resembling the Buddha's own qualities — the bodhisattvas of every ground below the Tathāgata's own resemble the Buddha's own qualities in essence and in enjoyment of their fruit; this is called partial resemblance. The Chapter Distinguishing Synonyms explains: "great child of the teacher" is the general term; "born from the womb" excludes ordinary beings and lesser, unworthy children; "born from the mouth" means born from the very voice proclaiming the dharma; "born from the dharma" means born from properly reflecting on and practising what was heard; "transformed by the dharma" means established through the path of the dharma-body, resembling the true dharma; "equal in portion of dharma" means enjoying the treasures of the uncontaminated dharma, resembling the true dharma.
Second, called the Bodhisattva Stage; first, stating the overall meaning. Thus fully and completely displaying every path a bodhisattva trains in and every fruit of that training is called the Bodhisattva Stage — fully explaining every bodhisattva's training path and its fruit, the true basis for every teaching of every kind.

items.title: Section: Four Other Names for the Bodhisattva Stage, and Merit Equal to the Great Vehicle's Own Scriptures

items.zh: 又此菩薩地，亦名菩薩藏摩怛理迦，亦名攝大乘，亦名開示壞不壞路，亦名無障智淨根本。若諸所有天人世間，或天、或人，若諸沙門、婆羅門等，於此所說菩薩地中，起堅信解、樂聞受持、精勤修學、廣為他說，下至書持、供養恭敬、深心愛重所得福聚；以要言之，如薄伽梵於菩薩藏所攝一切微妙經典樂聞等業，宣說、顯了、分別、施設、開示、稱讚所獲福聚，等無有異。
items.en:
This Bodhisattva Stage is also called the matrix of the bodhisattva basket, also called compendium of the Great Vehicle, also called revealing the destructible and indestructible path, and also called the root of pure, unobstructed wisdom.
Third, broadly praising the store of merit; first, stating the overall meaning. Whatever devas or humans, ascetics or brahmins, develop firm faith and understanding in this Bodhisattva Stage, delight in hearing and upholding it, diligently train in it, widely teach it to others, or even merely copy, revere, and cherish it deeply — in brief, the store of merit thereby gained is fully equal, without any difference, to the merit gained from delighting in, expounding, clarifying, distinguishing, formulating, revealing, and praising every wondrous sūtra contained within the bodhisattva basket that the Blessed One taught.

items.title: Section: A Retrospective Begins — Why Lineage Comes Before Aspiration, and the Eight Benefits of Arousing Bodhicitta

items.zh: 菩薩地顯示一切菩薩藏中，略標、廣釋諸門攝故。於此地中，能廣開示法毘柰耶，乃至眾多所化有情，於此正法受持讀誦、法隨法行，安住增長廣大勝進；於爾所時，像似正法不得興盛，正法不滅。若於爾時，像似正法當得興盛，即於爾時，能引實義所有正法當速滅沒。是故於此菩薩地中，起堅信解、樂聞受持，乃至廣說所得福聚無量無邊。如是已說菩薩地義。云何應知此中次第？謂諸菩薩要先安住菩薩種性，乃能正發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心。
items.en:
Within the basic section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the fourth yoga foundation of sequential practice, the chapter on arousing the aspiration for perfect awakening.
Second, the sequential meaning of the grounds; first, concluding what precedes and generating what follows. Thus the meaning of the Bodhisattva Stage has been explained. How should its sequence here be understood?
Second, distinguishing each in detail; first, distinguishing; first, what the first yoga foundation encompasses; first, lineage and arousal holding. Bodhisattvas must first abide securely in the bodhisattva lineage before they can rightly arouse the aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

blocks.text: The Bodhisattva Ground, the fifteenth of the seventeen stages and the longest part of the treatise so far, ends today. A retrospective then begins, retracing the whole path.
The three foundations of mindfulness. Venerable Miào Jìng: believe or not, the Buddha's mind remains pure.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha doesn't sleep; he is always in absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: whoever is ready to be taught, he appears to teach. Neutral matters are discerned and set aside through wisdom.

Bodhisattvas rely on these qualities to train, realise, and benefit all beings. Venerable Miào Jìng: arousing supreme bodhicitta is the correct vow. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha becomes a buddha through benefiting others.
Venerable Miào Jìng: only the Buddha has these qualities. (Ru-Yi misreads 有 here.)
Venerable Miào Jìng: the road of birth and death can be destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi adds: wrongly grasped emptiness, denying causation, is the destroying path in the bad sense.

One must first abide in the bodhisattva lineage. Venerable Miào Jìng: without it, bodhicitta cannot be established. Master Cháng Bǎi: from beginningless time the mind has the capacity for compassion and prajñā.

subs.head: Looking back on the Bodhisattva Ground

blocks.text: Begun in fascicle 35 (Day 304), the Bodhisattva Ground has taken nearly a hundred and fifty days. It moved from lineage and the first arousal of the mind, through the perfections and the factors of awakening, to the grounds, the marks, and the powers of a buddha.

quiz.q: Which qualities accomplish the fifth deed, a mind free of defilement?
quiz.why: The three foundations of mindfulness. Venerable Miào Jìng: believe or not, the Buddha's mind remains pure.

quiz.q: "Surveying the world day and night." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: he doesn't sleep, always in absorption; Cháng Bǎi: whoever is ripe, he manifests for
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha doesn't sleep; he is always in absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: whoever is ready to be taught, he appears to teach.

quiz.q: What does "discern and cast aside" mean in the tenth deed?
options: wisely discerning and setting aside what's neutral or meaningless, not without examination
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a wise decision, made through examination. Master Cháng Bǎi: neutral matters are discerned and set aside through wisdom.

quiz.q: Why is the Tathāgata's ground called "established"?
options: aspiring bodhisattvas rely on it to train, realise, and benefit all beings
quiz.why: Bodhisattvas rely on it to train, realise, and benefit all beings. Master Cháng Bǎi: they aspire towards these qualities, hence "established."

quiz.q: What does "aspiring" mean here, per the lectures?
options: relying on the great aspiration — Miào Jìng: arousing bodhicitta is the correct vow; Cháng Bǎi: vow leads practice
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: arousing supreme bodhicitta is the correct vow. Master Cháng Bǎi: the vow's power is the basis; vow guides practice.

quiz.q: Why do these qualities, according with benefiting others, exclude the two vehicles?
options: a buddha arises through benefiting others; the two vehicles seek self-benefit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha becomes buddha through benefiting others; the two vehicles seek their own benefit. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is where benefiting beings shows itself.

quiz.q: "獨一有義" is rendered "uniquely meaningful." How do the lectures read it?
options: "alone possessing" — only the Buddha has it; not "uniquely meaningful"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: only the Buddha has these qualities. Master Cháng Bǎi: only the Buddha has this accomplishment. The English misreads "有."

quiz.q: The stage is also called "revealing the destructible and indestructible path." How do the lectures explain?
options: Miào Jìng: delusion-karma-suffering is the road that can be destroyed; Cháng Bǎi adds: the "destroying path" is wrongly grasped emptiness, denying causation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the road of birth and death can be destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi agrees, and adds the reading that wrongly grasped emptiness, denying causation, is the destroying path.

quiz.q: What must come first for rightly arousing the aspiration?
quiz.why: One must first abide in the bodhisattva lineage. Venerable Miào Jìng: without it, bodhicitta cannot be established.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the lineage naturally present?
options: since beginningless time, a capacity for compassion and prajñā; "holding" keeps the seed until buddhahood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from beginningless time the mind has the capacity of compassion and prajñā; "holding" means the seed held until buddhahood.
